newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates fall in week - FHLMC.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates fall in week - FHLMC.

text.p: Interest rates on 15- and 30-year mortgages fell sharply this week from last week, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.
The agency, known as Freddie Mac, said the rate on 30-year, fixed-rate loans fell to 7.74 percent from 7.88 percent while 15-year loan rates dropped to 7.25 percent from 7.38 percent.
One-year adjustable-rate loans also edged lower to an average 5.51 percent from 5.55 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.02 percent, the 15-year rate stood at 6.51 percent and the one-year adjustable rate was 5.33 percent.
"As was expected, the Federal Reserve met Tuesday of this week and did not raise interest rates," Freddie Mac chief economist Robert Van Order said.
"This news, combined with a low inflation rate, helped keep interest rates low and affordable, which is where we expect them to stay for the near future at least," he said.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans, down from 1.8 percent last week. They charged 1.7 percent on 15-year loans, unchanged from last week, and 1.3 percent on adjustables, down from 1.4 percent the prior week.
